Effervescent

/ef-er-VES-ent/ - the stress falls on VES · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Effervescent means bubbly, lively.

The new intern's effervescent hello made even the Monday inventory count feel briefly like a party.

Worked Example

The morning traffic reporter is so effervescent that drivers stuck on the bridge call in just to banter — one sparkling minute with her, they say, and the jam feels shorter.

Effervescent is a soda-water word: it literally describes liquids that fizz, and by a happy leap, people whose liveliness fizzes the same way — light, bright, bubbling up in conversation. It is sparkle rather than force; for the full rolling boil, see this unit's ebullient.

How Effervescent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

bubbly

bubbly: the everyday word for the same fizz

sparkling

sparkling: bright and lively, with a hint of polish

Antonyms

flat

flat: the fizz gone — like day-old soda

dull

dull: no light in it at all

How Strong Is It? — mild → perky → effervescent

mild vs. effervescent

mild vs. effervescent: A mild manner is calm and low-key — pleasant enough, but far quieter than anything effervescent.

perky vs. effervescent

perky vs. effervescent: Perky is bright and alert, but it stops short of effervescent — perky nods along; effervescent fills the whole room with fizz.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ef-

Prefix — ef-: out (Latin ex-)

Root — ferv

Root — ferv: to boil, to be hot (Latin fervere)

Suffix — -escent

Suffix — -escent: beginning to, becoming (as in adolescent)

Put it together

Put it together: Ef- (out) + ferv- (to boil) + -escent (beginning to) = beginning to boil out — which is precisely what a fizzy drink does as the bubbles start their climb. Latin fervere, to boil, also heats this unit's fervent: the fervent believer and the effervescent hostess share one root and run at two temperatures.

Use the root in a new word: fervent

Use the root in a new word: fervent: He is a fervent defender of the oxford comma, with a bumper sticker to prove it.

Root Check

Word Choice

light / social

Effervescent praises social sparkle — charm that fizzes: quick wit, bright greetings, laughter that carries. It is lighter than this unit's ebullient, which boils rather than fizzes, and kinder than hyper. Champagne, soda water, and certain morning people: all effervescent.
